   173	  # is that Ctrl and Meta stay the terminal's -- emacs keys reach the shell --
   174	  # so no Ctrl- or Alt-only chord is left: not the Mac table's own
   175	  # (Ctrl+1..9 tab select, Alt+Z word wrap, Ctrl+PageUp/Down), not a Linux
   176	  # default. Only Ctrl+Tab stays, which the terminal receives as a bare Tab,
   177	  # and the few orcaPinned below puts back on purpose.
   178	  #
   179	  # Generated from the app's own keybinding definitions at build time
   180	  # (nix/orca-mac-keybindings.js), so a version bump picks up new actions.
   181	  # Chords Hyprland binds would be dead keys, so those actions are unbound --
   182	  # on shiori 19 of them, Super+F (find) and Super+P (go to file) among them,
   183	  # plus Super+B/N/E, the digits, and their Shift forms. orcaPinned below
   184	  # rebinds the ones worth having elsewhere. The build log lists every one.
   185	  #
   186	  # A running Orca reads the file once; after a switch, restart it (or run its
   187	  # keybindings reload) for the new table to apply. Resetting a generated
   188	  # shortcut in Orca's settings re-applies the Mac chord at the next switch:
   189	  # Orca stores a reset, and a pick of its own Linux default, as the same
   190	  # deletion, so neither sticks -- set some other chord, or unbind, instead.
   191	  #
   192	  # Find goes on Ctrl+S, emacs' isearch, everywhere but the terminal; there
   193	  # C-s is the shell's own search, so terminal search is left unbound.
   194	  #
   195	  # Previous/next worktree, in list order, on Alt+Up/Down: the Mac chord,
   196	  # Super+Shift+Up/Down, is Hyprland's. Orca catches it before any widget, so
   197	  # this takes M-<up>/<down> from the terminal and the editor's move-line too,
   198	  # deliberately.
   199	  orcaPinned = {
   200	    "editor.find" = [ "Ctrl+S" ];
   201	    "browser.find" = [ "Ctrl+S" ];
   202	    "chat.find" = [ "Ctrl+S" ];
   203	    "settings.search" = [ "Ctrl+S" ];
   204	    "worktree.navigateUp" = [ "Alt+ArrowUp" ];
   205	    "worktree.navigateDown" = [ "Alt+ArrowDown" ];
   206	  };
   207	  hyprlandChords = let s = config.wayland.windowManager.hyprland.settings; in
   208	    lib.concatMap
   209	      (k: map (b: if builtins.isAttrs b && b ? _args then builtins.head b._args else b) s.${k})
   210	      # bind, bindl, binde, ...: the lists. `binds` is a config section, a set.
   211	      (builtins.filter (k: lib.hasPrefix "bind" k && builtins.isList s.${k}) (builtins.attrNames s));
   212	  macKeybindings = pkgs.runCommand "orca-mac-keybindings" {
   213	    nativeBuildInputs = [ pkgs.nodejs pkgs.asar pkgs.makeWrapper pkgs.jq ];
   214	  } ''
   215	    asar extract ${appimageContents}/resources/app.asar app
   216	    mkdir -p $out/share $out/bin
   217	    node ${./nix/orca-mac-keybindings.js} app/out/shared \
   218	      ${pkgs.writeText "hyprland-chords.json" (builtins.toJSON hyprlandChords)} \
   219	      ${pkgs.writeText "orca-pinned.json" (builtins.toJSON orcaPinned)} \
   220	      > $out/share/orca-mac-keybindings.json
   221	    # The merge runs Orca's conflict check on the merged file at activation,
   222	    # so the keybinding module (and its one sibling import) ships alongside.
   223	    mkdir -p $out/lib/shared
   224	    cp -r app/out/shared/keybindings.js app/out/shared/keybindings \
   225	      app/out/shared/tui-agent-display-names.js $out/lib/shared/
   226	    makeWrapper ${pkgs.nodejs}/bin/node $out/bin/orca-mac-keybindings \
   227	      --add-flags "${./nix/orca-mac-keybindings-merge.js} $out/lib/shared $out/share/orca-mac-keybindings.json"
   228	    # One real merge, so an Orca bump that moves an import or an export the
   229	    # merge uses fails here, not as a warning at every activation. The seed
   230	    # is a string (comma-list) value, so the shorthand parser runs too; it
   231	    # sits on a New-agent-tab action, unbound on every platform, so the
   232	    # table never claims it whatever Hyprland binds. The check is that every
   233	    # generated entry landed as generated, and the seed survived.
   234	    mkdir -p $TMPDIR/home/.orca
   235	    echo '{"version":1,"keybindings":{},"platforms":{"linux":{"tab.newAgent.claude":"Alt+F12, Alt+Shift+F12"}}}' \
   236	      > $TMPDIR/home/.orca/keybindings.json
   237	    HOME=$TMPDIR/home $out/bin/orca-mac-keybindings 2> merge.err
   238	    if [ -s merge.err ] \
   239	       || ! jq -e --slurpfile o $out/share/orca-mac-keybindings.json '
   240	            .platforms.linux as $l
   241	            | ($o[0] | to_entries | all(.value == $l[.key]))
   242	              and $l["tab.newAgent.claude"] == "Alt+F12, Alt+Shift+F12"' \
   243	            $TMPDIR/home/.orca/keybindings.json >/dev/null \
   244	       || [ ! -s $TMPDIR/home/.orca/keybindings.nix-owned.json ]; then
   245	      cat merge.err >&2; echo "orca: build-time merge did not apply the table" >&2; exit 1
   246	    fi
   247	  '';
   248	  # ~/.orca/keybindings.json is Orca's read-write state: its settings UI saves
   249	  # into the same platforms.linux section, by atomic rename, so a home.file
   250	  # symlink would be replaced on the first edit. So the generated keys are
   251	  # merged into whatever Orca last wrote, owning only what the last merge
   252	  # wrote (a sidecar records it), and a UI edit outranks them -- the rules
   253	  # are at the top of nix/orca-mac-keybindings-merge.js.
   254	  # tests/orca-mac-keybindings.sh.
   255	in
   256	{
   257	  home.packages =
   258	    lib.optionals (!isDarwin && isDesktop) [ orcaGui orcaCli ];
   259	
   260	  home.file = lib.mkIf (!isDarwin && isDesktop) (lib.listToAttrs (map (name: {
   261	    name = ".claude/skills/${name}";
   262	    value.source = "${orcaSkillsSrc}/skills/${name}";
   263	  }) orcaSkills));
   264	
   265	  home.activation.orcaMacKeybindings = lib.mkIf (!isDarwin && isDesktop)
   266	    (lib.hm.dag.entryAfter [ "writeBoundary" ] ''
   267	      $DRY_RUN_CMD ${macKeybindings}/bin/orca-mac-keybindings
   268	    '');
   269	}

Contents of /home/sauyon/devel/dotfiles/.drovr/wt/orca-cli-node/CLAUDE.md:

## NO EMAILS

**Never write an email address into anything.** Not into files, commit messages,
docs, notes, handoffs or scratch files — mine, colleagues', or service accounts.
This repo is public, and an address is a durable identifier that spreads: it
leaks the work/personal boundary, it enumerates people, and once written it gets
copied onward.

Refer to an account by its **role** — "the personal Google account", "the work
account", "the project's GCS service agent" — or record the command that
recovers the identity at read time (`gcloud config get-value account`) rather
than pasting its output. Role-based wording is better documentation anyway: "must
be the personal account, not the work one" survives an address change; a pasted
address does not.

If an address seems genuinely load-bearing, ask first.

The exception is the git identity already configured in `home.nix`, which git
requires and which is on every commit regardless.

## Commit and Push Policy

This is a personal dotfiles repo on `master`. When asked to commit and push, do both without asking for confirmation. The global "ask before public communications" rule does not apply here.

## Applying config: use `hms`, not `home-manager switch`

`hms` (defined in `home.nix`, documented in `README.md`) pushes, waits for the
commit's CI run on `forge.ko.ag`, then switches — so the switch is a download of
the closure the in-cluster runner built, not a local compile. Expect it to block
for ten-odd minutes. `hms --local` builds here instead.

It refuses on a dirty tree and on a diverged checkout — **both refusals are
the feature.** CI can only build a pushed commit, so do not route around them
with a bare `home-manager switch` — commit and push, or pass `--local`
deliberately and say that you did.

A checkout on master that is strictly behind `origin/master` fast-forwards to
the fetched SHA and continues — no refusal, nothing to decide.

If a run goes red, `hms` prints the job's `error:` lines; read those rather than
re-running blind. Background on why CI is worth waiting for — and the 600s attic
transfer ceiling that made it unreliable for its first 61 runs — is in
`docs/ci-nix-home.md`.

</system-reminder>

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Why: invoked via ~/.local/bin/orca-ide symlink (from CliInstaller); resolve it
# so APP_DIR points at the real install, not the symlink's parent.
SOURCE="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
while [ -h "$SOURCE" ]; do
	DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$SOURCE")" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)"
	SOURCE="$(readlink "$SOURCE")"
	[[ $SOURCE != /* ]] && SOURCE="$DIR/$SOURCE"

Round 2 review of `origin/master..HEAD` (53132d82 + merge) in /home/sauyon/devel/dotfiles/.drovr/wt/orca-cli-node. I read the diff, the commit log, nix-eval.yml, the built wrapper and bwrap launcher (/nix/store/rzvfq0zd2dx43ffidnkjagqjp46088za-orca-1.4.238), and the CLI source in the extracted AppImage. I launched nothing.

## Critical
None.

## Important

**I1. tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:76 and :86-88 — if node mode regresses, the test can leave an Orca running, and line 76 can hang.**
- The built launcher calls bwrap with no `--unshare-pid` and, after this branch, no `--die-with-parent`. bwrap's sandboxed child therefore outlives bwrap.
- On line 76, `timeout 60` signals only bwrap, so it does not stop the payload. On line 86 the payload has no timeout at all.
- While `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1` gets through, both payloads exit on their own: `-p` exits at once, and the `-e` script calls `process.exit` at 5s. Normal runs and early `exit 1` paths leave nothing behind. An `exit 1` at :97 just makes the payload's write fail, and it still exits.
- The leak is the case where node mode is not honoured: the env var is dropped by a wrapper layer, or the RunAsNode fuse gets disabled. Electron then starts the real GUI with `-p '"node-ok"'` or `-e …` as argv:
  - On line 76 it survives `timeout 60`. It also holds the write end of the `$(...)` stdout pipe, so the test blocks until that GUI exits.
  - On line 86 it simply keeps running.
  - The wrapper adds no wayland flag when `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE` is set, so on an X-less Hyprland session the GUI probably exits 1 by itself. With Xwayland, or on CI, nothing guarantees that.
- Cheap fixes:
  - Skip the lifetime case when the node-mode probe fails.
  - Run each payload with `--new-session`/`setsid` and kill its process group (or a recorded pid) in the EXIT trap.
  - Redirect line 76's stdout to a file in `$T`, not a pipe.

## nit

- **orca.nix:65** — `*" --ozone-platform"*` also matches `--ozone-platform-hint=…` and anything after `--`. Upstream's own check (`out/shared/headless-serve-ozone-platform.js` `hasExplicitOzonePlatform`) says a hint "is only a preference", stops at `--`, and matches only `--ozone-platform` / `--ozone-platform=`. So the wrapper drops the wayland default in cases where Orca's gate would still pick X11. Match `" --ozone-platform "` / `" --ozone-platform="*`.
- **orca.nix:43-44** — "appimageTools keeps the AppImage's own bin name, so the wrapper is written by hand" no longer gives the real reason. A rename alone could be an `mv`. The wrapper is hand-written because the flag is conditional (on node mode and on a caller-supplied flag), which `makeShellWrapper --add-flags` cannot express.
- **orca.nix:60** — "orca-ide-app execs it, the flag first" reads as unconditional. Lines 51-55 qualify it, so this is minor; "the flag first unless …" would fix it.
- **orca.nix:116-118** — "Orca's own installer only reaches an Orca terminal (… and a ~/.local/bin symlink …)": `~/.local/bin` is usually on PATH outside Orca terminals too. The point is that the symlink targets a raw store path and goes stale, as the test header (lines 8-10) says. Worth wording it the same way here.
- **tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:84-85** — the lifetime case goes red under `dieWithParent = true` only if bwrap arms PDEATHSIG within 2s. On a very slow runner a regression could pass. The comment already admits this; widening `sleep 2` (and the 4s/5s timers) would add margin cheaply.
- **tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:33 vs orca.nix:165-168** — the skill list is duplicated. A skill dropped from orca.nix fails the test (good). A skill added to orca.nix is never hash-checked. Deriving the list from `home.file` attr names under `.claude/skills/` (minus the repo's own skills) or from orca.nix would close that.
- **tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:142** — `sha256sum -c` checks only files the manifest lists; extra or stale files in the skill dir are not caught. Harmless for a pinned fetch, but the header says "the bytes this Orca build expects".
- **tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:138** — the `nix-store --realise "$srcdrv"` result is not checked. A failure shows up as "<src> is missing", which hides the real cause.

## Checked and fine
- **Comments vs code:**
  - The `dieWithParent` rationale (orca.nix:35-37) holds: the nixGL wrapper does `exec -a`, orca-ide-app `exec`s, and the launcher `exec`s bwrap.
  - "Electron serve appends --ozone-platform=x11" (orca.nix:55) is right: `childArgs.push(...)` at the end, launch.js:160.
  - "without it `open` fails and `serve` refuses" (orca.nix:120-122) is right: `launchOrcaApp` throws `runtime_open_failed`, and `resolveForegroundOrcaExecutable` throws the server-only message.
  - The NODE_OPTIONS handoff matches upstream's resources/bin/orca-ide line for line.
  - `sourceCommit:\`e6f7fba…\`` occurs once in app.asar.
  - Under plain node the CLI reads version and commit from out/package.json in app.asar.unpacked, so `--version` and `skills install` work.
  - The old "Wrap the AppImage (not autoPatchelf…)" text is untouched, as instructed.
- **No hidden launches:** the CLI commands the test runs (`--version`, `skills get`, an unknown command) never call `launchOrcaApp`; only `open` does.
- **Secrets:** nothing prints env.
  - `outside()` unsets every `ORCA_*` (including ORCA_AGENT_HOOK_TOKEN) for the CLI cases.
  - Failure messages print only CLI output, `ls`, or the last stderr line of the node probe.
  - The GUI payloads (76, 86) inherit the token but print nothing of it.
  - No `set -x`.
- **Test validity:** each case goes red on a regression of its claim:
  - wayland flag in node mode → node exits 9 → empty output → FAIL
  - `dieWithParent = true` → payload killed at 2s, before it writes at 4s
  - wrong ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE → string mismatch
  - non-exec wrapper → exit-status / plain-exec checks
  - rev/version skew → sourceCommit grep
  - skill drift → manifest sha256 check
- **CI viability:** every tool used is in the nix-eval.yml shell (coreutils incl. timeout/seq/paste/sha256sum, grep, sed, jq, nix-store). `/etc/hostname` is written by CI, and the `uname -n` fallback is harmless. bwrap without user or pid namespaces runs as root in the privileged container, the same way tests/sandbox-fonts.sh already runs the launcher. `/tmp` is bound into the FHS env, so `$T/alive` is reachable.
- **tests/sandbox-fonts.sh:** the name regex `.*orca-[0-9.]+` does not match `orca-cli-1.4.238`. `.orca-ide-unwrapped` is still in the closure, and its line-43 comment is still accurate.
- **Security:** the skills come from a fetch pinned by hash, with the rev in the store name. Per-file `home.file` keys do not collide with home.nix's `.claude/skills/{linear-flow,agy-review,…}`. The `ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE` override is caller-controlled env, as upstream allows.
